comments.content: containedScopeTarget canonicalization gap: `root` is never resolved via realpath, so `path.relative(root, real)` is wrong when `root` itself contains a symlink (e.g. /tmp -> /private/tmp on macOS) — legitimate scopes falsely return null (fail-closed availability loss). Worse, the function returns unresolved `target` instead of `real`, so downstream `statSync/walk` operate on a symlink-containing path while the containment verdict was computed on the resolved path (TOCTOU/aliasing). Fix: `const canonRoot = fs.realpathSync(root)` (fallback to root) for the relative check and return `real` on success.

Unguarded content-hash recompute breaks fail-closed discipline: if `computeSourceHash` throws (fd open/read/close failure, EMFILE, EACCES race), the exception escapes `isGraphifyCheckoutFreshFor` instead of returning a named stale verdict, and bubbles through `populateFromGraphifyCheckout` as a rejected promise rather than `{ok:false, reason: GRAPHIFY_NOT_WARM:...}`. Wrap in try/catch and return `{fresh:false, reason:'stale-hash-error'}`.

TOCTOU size race can falsely report fresh: `size` comes from a pre-open `statSync`, then `Buffer.alloc(size)` + single `readSync` assumes it is still valid. If the file grows between stat and open (small-file branch), the new tail is silently ignored with no marker (read==size, no short-read marker) and collides with the pre-edit digest. Fix: `fstatSync(fd)` after open and hash the authoritative size, or loop reads and mark growth.

First-run freshness bypass seeds a new store from a stale graph: when `storePath` is absent the probe is skipped (`first-run` => fresh) even if `graph.json`/sidecar is weeks old. "Nothing to be stale" is wrong — the new rows are stale. The warm-miss path should still run `isGraphifyCheckoutFreshFor` on first run (only the `absent` graph case already fails closed via the adapter's GRAPHIFY_NOT_WARM). Remove the bypass or treat first-run identical to the normal probe.
comments.suggestion_code: const freshness = isGraphifyCheckoutFreshFor(resolvedRoot, graphPath, pinned.graph?.scope ?? ["src"], pinned.graph?.excludes ?? []);

comments.content: Post-commit sidecar rehash introduces a stale-wins window: the hash is recomputed AFTER the DB COMMIT by re-walking the live tree. An edit landing between the pre-populate freshness check and this write makes the sidecar describe post-edit sources while `graph.json` is pre-edit, so the next probe matches and serves a stale graph as fresh. The sidecar must be written by the builder (scripts/graphify-build.ts) at build time, or the pre-check digest must be reused — never rehash mutable sources after commit.

Checkout/session parity drift: session `supersedeThenInsert` refuses only when BOTH tables are empty (edges-only allowed), but `writeGraphifyCheckout` throws on `nodeRows.length===0` even with non-empty edges. Checkout also skips `gi_meta` writes, omits `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000` that `openTypedStore` sets, and uses `Date.now()` for the default runTag (same-ms collisions). Align the empty-guard, write the same meta keys, set busy_timeout, and use `randomUUID()`/counter for runTag.
comments.suggestion_code: if (nodeRows.length === 0 && edgeRows.length === 0) throw new Error("GRAPH_EMPTY:graphify checkout refusing empty input (would wipe live inspection rows)");
comments.existing_code: if (nodeRows.length === 0) throw new Error("GRAPH_EMPTY:graphify checkout refusing empty input (would wipe live inspection rows)");

comments.content: Byte-unbounded hashing + magic-number drift: `computeSourceHash` hardcodes `500` instead of `GRAPHIFY_FRESHNESS_BUDGET`, so changing the budget silently desyncs the mtime walk from the hash walk (stale-budget vs budget-exhausted marker mismatch). Worse, the budget counts files not bytes — 500 files x 8MB streamed whole = ~4GB I/O per probe, twice per populate (check + sidecar write). Use the exported constant and add a total-byte cap; also dedupe the repeated skip-list + extension regex into shared constants.
